bug_report_content:
id: 931
status: Fixed
summary: arguments is moved to another scope
labels: ['Type-Defect', 'Priority-Medium']
stars: 0
commentCount: 6
Comment 0 (2013-02-26): Using ADVANCED_OPTIMIZATIONS with CompilerOptions.collapsePropertiesOnExternTypes = true a script I used broke, it was something like: function () { return function () { var arg = arguments; setTimeout(function() { alert(args); }, 0); } } Unfortunately it was rewritten to: function () { return function () { setTimeout(function() { alert(arguments); }, 0); } } arguments should not be collapsed.
Comment 1 (2013-02-26): Can you provide an exact snippet, I'm not able to reproduce this problem. Also, note that code that you provide here has a typo ("arg" vs. "args"). CompilerOptions.collapsePropertiesOnExternTypes should also have nothing to do with inlining variables.
Comment 2 (2013-02-27): Yeah, we almost always model "arguments" as "a global variable that can change over time." If there was a bug where a local alias "arguments" was getting inlined, then it's likely that bug would affect all global variables, and some project would have run into it by now. I suspect that you did see a bug, but that you mis-diagnosed what triggered it... and in an attempt to simplify the repro steps, you edited out the trigger.
Comment 3 (2013-02-27): I've added an example of this behavior in the following repository: https://github.com/robbert/closure-compiler/tree/issue-931 The following commit contains one build with and one without the flag set to true: issue-931/jQueryDeferred.min.js issue-931/jQueryDeferred.min-collapsePropertiesOnExternTypes.js https://github.com/robbert/closure-compiler/commit/bf59bcf89262c76de9ab6e75599bdba0291a31cf Excerpt of collapsePropertiesOnExternTypes = true: function C() { var a = D; return function() { console.log("This is were arguments originally is defined"); var b = new p; this.d.then(function(d) { var c = d[a]; console.log("This is it ends up"); c = c.apply(d, arguments); c instanceof p ? c.then(z(b, b.resolve), z(b, b.reject)) : c instanceof A ? c.d.then(z(b, b.resolve), z(b, b.reject)) : b.resolve(c); return c }, B); return new A(b) } } Without that flag, arguments is on the fifth line as it is supposed to: function C() { var a = D; return function() { console.log("This is were arguments originally is defined"); var b = arguments, d = new p; this.d.then(function(c) { var f = c[a]; console.log("This is it ends up"); c = f.apply(c, b); c instanceof p ? c.then(z(d, d.resolve), z(d, d.reject)) : c instanceof A ? c.d.then(z(d, d.resolve), z(d, d.reject)) : d.resolve(c); return c }, B); return new A(d) } }
Comment 4 (2013-02-27): Thank you for the detailed reproduction steps, I was able to reproduce this.
Comment 5 (2013-02-27): This issue was closed by revision 9fac3ccd2fa9.
